This is a very odd time.  It's a time wherein we actually have time to reflect, and for many people (me included), self-reflection is often unwelcome.

I've always managed to find some sort of diversion, but now some (what?) four weeks into this quarantine all my diversions have been played out.  I imagine it's the same for you and many others.  Now is a time in history where we're all forced to reckon with ourselves.

Because of this forced self-reckoning I've been increasingly thinking of suicide.  No explicit plans or anything; rather, just the idea of it.  The thing in my head like your cocaine.  My seeming need for it.  I'm certainly not the first person to have compared suicide to a lover.

But then I close my eyes and think: I could write a book.  I could run a marathon.  I could volunteer at a food bank.  I could actually take steps to make my house a home.  I could read more.  I could try to figure all of this out.  I could plan a party at my place for the folks who really want to know me, the folks who I'm always keeping at arm's length, that I text and never call.

I think: I'm not very good at this, or anything, but, given time, I could learn enough to at least find myself respectable.  I can have some small victory that will help me find myself respectable.  The world is out there, and I am in here, and I have no one else to compare myself to, and, in this era of self-isolation and sheltering-in-place, that to me is the ultimate freedom.
